title: nginx access / error log signals
description: Patterns covering nginx access-log 5xx and error-log entries that map to critical infrastructure issues (upstream failures, permission errors, disconnects).

patterns.name: 5xx response
patterns.explanation: An HTTP 5xx response was logged, indicating a server-side request failure.
patterns.severityRationale: Warning because the request failed, but the broad status-code match does not identify the root cause.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Intentional error tests, health-check probes, and isolated client requests can return 5xx.

patterns.name: upstream connect timeout
patterns.explanation: nginx could not connect to or receive a timely response from an upstream service.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because the edge path cannot reliably serve requests from its backend.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Deploy drains, overloaded test backends, and planned maintenance can create transient timeouts.

examples.positive: upstream timed out while reading response header

patterns.name: permission denied
patterns.explanation: nginx or its upstream path was denied access to a requested resource.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because a permission boundary is blocking the web service from completing its operation.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Expected ACLs, sandboxing, and probing a protected path can emit this message.

patterns.name: client disconnected prematurely
patterns.explanation: The client closed or disconnected before nginx finished the request.
patterns.severityRationale: Notice because the request was abandoned, but the server may be healthy.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Browsers cancelling navigation, client timeouts, and network churn are common causes.

notes: Order does not matter; severity tie-breaks go to the leftmost pattern. The 5xx regex matches both access and error lines.
